exercises.heading: 10.4. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1, 2, 3, and 4 Find the area of the region that is bounded by the given curve and lies in the specified sector.
5, 6, 7, and 8 Find the area of the shaded region.

problem.paragraph: 5. Details A closed curve with two loops labeled r^2 = sin(2 theta) is graphed on a coordinate plane. The curve resembles an infinity symbol with its arms in the first and third quadrants. The loop in the first quadrant is shaded. $$\frac{1}{2}$$

6. Details A closed curve labeled r = 2 + cos(theta) is graphed on a coordinate plane. The curve resembles a cardioid without the cusp but a flattened side on the left. The portion of the curve on the right of the vertical axis is much larger than the portion on the left. The area within the curve in the second quadrant is shaded.

7. Details A cardioid with its cusp opening downward is labeled r = 4 + 3 sin(theta) and it is graphed on a coordinate plane. The cusp is a slight upward bulge, reaching its high point on the negative vertical axis. The cardioid is symmetric about the vertical axis and the portion of the cardioid on the right of the vertical axis is shaded. $$\frac{41}{4}\pi$$

8. Details A spiral and a shaded region labeled r = sqrt(In theta), 1 less than or equal to theta which is less than or equal to 2 pi are graphed on a coordinate plane. The spiral makes a full revolution and reaches the positive horizontal axis. The region bound by the spiral and the positive horizontal axis is shaded.

exercises.instruction: 9, 10, 11, and 12 Sketch the curve and find the area that it encloses.
13, 14, 15, and 16 Graph the curve and find the area that it encloses.
17, 18, 19, 20, and 21 Find the area of the region enclosed by one loop of the curve.

problem.paragraph: Find the area enclosed by the loop of the strophoid $$r = 2\cos\theta - \sec\theta$$ .

exercises.instruction: 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, and 28 Find the area of the region that lies inside the first curve and outside the second curve.
29, 30, 31, 32, 33, and 34 Find the area of the region that lies inside both curves.

problem.paragraph: Find the area inside the larger loop and outside the smaller loop of the limaçon $$r = \frac{1}{2} + \cos\theta$$ .
Find the area between a large loop and the enclosed small loop of the curve $$r = 1 + 2\cos 3\theta$$ .

exercises.instruction: 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, and 42 Find all points of intersection of the given curves.
43, 44, 45, and 46 Find the area of the shaded region.

problem.paragraph: 43. Details A cardioid labeled r = 3 + 2 cos(theta), a four-leaved rose labeled r = sin(2 theta), and a shaded region are graphed on a coordinate plane. The cardioid is symmetric about the horizontal axis and has its cusp opening leftward on the negative horizontal axis. A small four-leaved rose with its leaves in the four quadrants is centered at the origin. The region within the cardioid excluding the four leaves of the rose is shaded. $$21\pi \slash 2$$

44. Details Two curves and a shaded region are graphed on a coordinate plane. The first curve, labeled r^2 = sqrt(3) sin(2 theta), resembles an infinity symbol with its arms in the first and third quadrants. The second curve labeled r = sqrt(2) cos(theta), is a circle symmetric about the positive horizontal axis and its leftmost point touches the origin. The region bound by the loop of the first curve and the part of the circle in the first quadrant is shaded.

45. Details A cardioid, a circle, and a shaded region are graphed on a coordinate plane. The cardioid is labeled r = 1 + cos(theta), has its cusp opening leftward and the pointed end of the cusp is at the origin. A circle, labeled r = 3 cos(theta), is symmetric about the positive horizontal axis with its leftmost point at the origin. The area between the top left of the circle and the top left of the cardioid is shaded. $$\pi \slash 8$$

46. Details A limaçon with an inner loop is graphed on a coordinate plane. The limaçon, labeled r = 1 minus 2 sin(theta), is symmetric about the vertical axis, with its cusp opening upward and the pointed end of the cusp at the origin. The limaçon has an inner loop symmetric about the negative vertical axis. The area within the limaçon excluding the loop is shaded.

The points of intersection of the cardioid $$r = 1 + \sin\theta$$ and the spiral loop $$r = 2\theta$$ , $$- \pi \slash 2 \leqslant \theta \leqslant \pi \slash 2$$ , can’t be found exactly. Use a graphing device to find the approximate values of $$\theta$$ at which they intersect. Then use these values to estimate the area that lies inside both curves.

When recording live performances, sound engineers often use a microphone with a cardioid pickup pattern because it suppresses noise from the audience. Suppose the microphone is placed $$4$$ m from the front of the stage (as in the figure) and the boundary of the optimal pickup region is given by the cardioid $$r = 8 + 8\sin\theta$$ , where $$r$$ is measured in meters and the microphone is at the pole. The musicians want to know the area they will have on stage within the optimal pickup range of the microphone. Answer their question.

image.alt: Details A cardioid, a horizontal line, and a shaded region are displayed. A horizontal line separates two regions. The upper region is labeled stage and the lower region is labeled audience. A cardioid with its cusp opening downward is positioned such that approximately two-thirds of the cardioid lies above the horizontal line. The height of the cardioid above the line is 12 meters. A point on the pointed end of the cusp is labeled microphone and it is 4 meters below the horizontal line. The portion of the cardioid above the horizontal line is shaded.

exercises.instruction: 49, 50, 51, and 52 Find the exact length of the polar curve.
53–54 Find the exact length of the portion of the curve shown in blue.

problem.paragraph: 53. Details A cardioid with its cusp opening downward is graphed on a coordinate plane. The cardioid is labeled r = 3 + 3 sin(theta), with the pointed end of its cusp at the origin. The portion of the curve in the first, second, and fourth quadrants is in blue. $$6\sqrt{2} + 12$$

54. Details A spiral is graphed on a coordinate plane. The spiral, labeled r = theta + 2, begins at the tick mark 2 on the horizontal axis, completes one and a half revolutions, and stops just before reaching the negative vertical axis. The one and a half revolutions of the spiral are in blue.

exercises.instruction: 55–56 Find the exact length of the curve. Use a graph to determine the parameter interval.
57–58 Set up, but do not evaluate, an integral to find the length of the portion of the curve shown in blue.

problem.paragraph: 57. Details A function labeled r = cos(theta/5), resembling a limaçon stuck to a circle is graphed on a coordinate plane. The limaçon with an inner loop is symmetric about the horizontal axis and has its cusp opening rightward and the pointed end of the cusp is on the positive horizontal axis. The broad end of the loop is at the origin. A circle is symmetric about the horizontal axis with its center at the origin. Its left-most point coincides with the leftmost point of the limaçon. The limaçon part of the curve is in blue. $$\int_{\pi}^{4\pi}\sqrt{\cos^{2}(\theta/5) + \frac{1}{25}\sin^{2}(\theta/5)}d\theta$$

58. Details A spiral, labeled r = sin(theta)/theta, is graphed on a coordinate plane. The spiral resembles the spiral on a conch. It has two very small circles, a small circle with its bottom-most points at the origin and a larger wing of the spiral that begins from the origin and meets the positive x-axis at a certain distance from the origin. The portion of the large wing of the spiral in the second quadrant and the half of the small circle in the first quadrant are in blue.

exercises.instruction: 59, 60, 61, and 62 Use a calculator or computer to find the length of the curve correct to four decimal places. If necessary, graph the curve to determine the parameter interval.
63, 64, 65, 66, 67, and 68 Find the slope of the tangent line to the given polar curve at the point specified by the value of $$\theta$$ .
69, 70, 71, and 72 Find the points on the given curve where the tangent line is horizontal or vertical.

problem.paragraph: Let $$P$$ be any point (except the origin) on the curve $$r = f(\theta)$$ . If $$\psi$$ is the angle between the tangent line at $$P$$ and the radial line $$OP$$ , show that

image.alt: Details A ray and two lines are displayed. The ray runs horizontally rightward. From a point O on the ray, a line slopes gradually upward to the right at an angle theta measured counterclockwise from the horizontal ray. A curve labeled r = f(theta), enters from the top, descends downward, bulging to the right, crossing the slanted line at a point labeled P. Another line slopes steeply upward to the right, to the right of the first line, at an angle phi from the horizontal ray and is tangent to the curve at the point P. Angle between the two lines at P is labeled Psi.

list.item: Use Exercise 73 to show that the angle between the tangent line and the radial line is $$\psi = \pi \slash 4$$ at every point on the curve $$r = e^{\theta}$$ .
Illustrate part (a) by graphing the curve and the tangent lines at the points where $$\theta = 0$$ and $$\pi \slash 2$$ .

Prove that any polar curve $$r = f(\theta)$$ with the property that the angle $$\psi$$ between the radial line and the tangent line is a constant must be of the form $$r = Ce^{ k\theta}$$ , where $$C$$ and $$k$$ are constants.

Use Formula 10.2.9 to show that the area of the surface generated by rotating the polar curve $$r = f(\theta) a \leqslant \theta \leqslant b$$ (where $$f^{\prime}$$ is continuous and $$0 \leqslant a < b \leqslant \pi$$ ) about the polar axis is $$S = {\int_{a}^{b}{2\pi r\sin\theta\sqrt{r^{2} + \left( \frac{dr}{d\theta} \right)^{2}}d\theta}}$$
Use the formula in part (a) to find the surface area generated by rotating the lemniscate $$r^{2} = \cos 2\theta$$ about the polar axis.

Find a formula for the area of the surface generated by rotating the polar curve $$r = f(\theta),a \leqslant \theta \leqslant b$$ (where $$f^{\prime}$$ is continuous and $$0 \leqslant a < b \leqslant \pi$$ ), about the line $$\theta = \pi \slash 2$$ .
Find the surface area generated by rotating the lemniscate $$r^{2} = \cos 2\theta$$ about the line $$\theta = \pi \slash 2$$ .
